key_insight: A hybrid LLM-guided search loop can effectively propose quantum reservoir architectures, but its benefit comes from being embedded in a constrained, reproducible optimization framework rather than from the LLM alone.
engineering_relevance: The work turns quantum reservoir design into a practical black-box architecture search problem, offering a template for using AI assistants to automate near-term quantum ML system tuning.
method: Benchmark QRC architecture search with five policies: random, evolutionary, Bayesian/TPE, feedback LLM, and a hybrid LLM-based controller.
Search over key design choices including input encoding, reservoir depth, entanglement topology, measurement features, reset policy, feature construction, and readout regularization.
Use memory, mutation, crossover, duplicate avoidance, and exploration to strengthen LLM proposals in the hybrid policy.
evidence_signal: Across NARMA10, Mackey-Glass, and temporal parity under a 25-evaluation budget and three seeds, the hybrid policy was most consistent, ranking first on two tasks and improving over random search on all tasks, including a 23.6% relative error reduction on Mackey-Glass.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific and do not demonstrate that LLMs are universally superior optimizers for quantum reservoir design; performance depends on the surrounding search protocol and evaluation budget.
paper_title: Hybrid LLM-Guided Search for Quantum Reservoir Architecture Design
